strings.name: Gilberto Gil
strings.role: Singer · songwriter · former Brazilian culture minister
strings.summary: Raised in Bahia, Gil combines Brazilian styles, rock, African music and reggae and helped shape Tropicália with Caetano Veloso and others. Detained under military rule and exiled in London, he returned to recording and performance in Brazil. A Salvador councilor and culture minister from 2003 to 2008, he advanced public- and digital-culture debate. He joined the Brazilian Academy of Letters in 2022 and ended the large-scale Tempo Rei farewell tour in 2026, leaving room for individual shows.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through November 13, 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: He participated in Tropicália and continues blending Brazilian and world music, while his cultural-policy work advanced public cultural issues.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.f1.value: Salvador, Bahia, Brazil; spent part of childhood in Ituaçu.
strings.facts.f2.label: Education and beginnings
strings.facts.f2.value: Completed business-administration studies at the Federal University of Bahia in 1964, working in business before focusing on music.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Musical fusion and Tropicália
strings.highlights.h1.text: Combined Brazilian, African, rock and reggae elements, extending Brazilian music’s international reach.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Cultural policy and public service
strings.highlights.h2.text: As councilor and culture minister, participated in public culture, digital culture and social-participation debates.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Ended large-scale Tempo Rei tour
strings.timeline.t1.text: Completed the farewell tour in São Paulo, retaining recording and individual performances rather than leaving music entirely.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Joined Brazilian Academy of Letters
strings.timeline.t2.text: Took seat 20 in recognition of poetic expression and cultural contribution.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Left culture ministry
strings.timeline.t3.text: Ended ministerial work begun in 2003 and refocused on music and public cultural activity.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Became culture minister
strings.timeline.t4.text: Accepted Lula’s invitation, working on cultural policy, digital culture and social participation.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Named UNESCO Artist for Peace
strings.timeline.t5.text: Received international recognition for music and public cultural activity.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Returned to Brazil from exile
strings.timeline.t6.text: Returned from London and released Expresso 2222, continuing musical fusion.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Went into exile in Britain
strings.timeline.t7.text: After detention, left Brazil with Veloso; London experiences influenced later recordings.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Joined Tropicália collective album
strings.timeline.t8.text: Recorded with Veloso and others; was detained by the military regime later that year.
strings.timeline.t9.title: Released Louvação
strings.timeline.t9.text: An important early album combined Brazilian traditions with his songwriting.
